newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks scale back losses, helped by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks scale back losses, helped by Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed slightly lower on Monday, well off earlier lows after traders took heart from a recovery on Wall Street and in bonds, dealers said.
The general index fell 1.12 points, 0.27 percent, to 407.07 and the Ibex shed 9.93 points, 0.21 percent, to 4,704.11.
BCH bank ended down 20 pesetas at 3,180 after Standard & Poor's downgraded the bank's short- and long-term ratings on Thursday, but revised up its outlook to stable from negative.

Telecoms equipment firm Amper posted a 5.87 percent gain to 2,165 pesetas. Dealers were unable to give any specific reason for the strong rise, although some related it to the recent sale of some of its assets to German group Siemens.

Overall, today Madrid caught up with sharp falls on world bourses on Friday, which was a public holiday in Spain. Traders had been unnerved by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning of "irrational exuberance" in asset markets.
But a firmer start today in New York after what was seen as an overreaction provided a tonic, while there was little domestic news to move Madrid shares independently, dealers said.
